 Bri Davis, Aspyn Ovard, Salomé Andrew and Bobbi Althoff are seen on an episode of “The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County,” a spinoff of the original Hulu series “The Secret Wives of Mormon Wives.” All eight episodes of the first season arrived on Hulu on Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026. (Disney/Ashley Rose)
 By Peter Larsen | plarsen@scng.com PUBLISHED: November 11, 2026 at 9:00 PM PST | UPDATED: November 11, 2026 at 9:31 PM PST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... When “The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” debuted on Hulu two years ago, in addition to taking viewers inside the familiar messy marriages of reality TV, the show also introduced viewers to a new vocabulary of terms such as MomTok, soft swinging, and dirty sodas .
 The original series was based in Utah, and it quickly spun off stars such as Whitney Leavett, who appeared on “Dancing With the Stars” and was cast as Roxie Hart in “Chicago” on Broadway, and Taylor Frankie Paul, was set to be “The Bachelorette” earlier this year before her personal scandal scuttled the season.
 Now comes the inevitable spinoff. Just as the success of “The Real Housewives of Orange County” led to “The Real Housewives of New York City,” the popularity of the original “Mormon Wives” now leads to “The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County.”
 All eight episodes of the new series arrive on Hulu on Nov. 12. In what surely can’t be a coincidence, it’s the same day as the final episode of Season 20 of “The Real Housewives of Orange County.”

(Disney/Ashley Rose) Expand 
 We watched the first two episodes of “Mormon Wives: Orange County,” and we’re here to help you get to know the brand-new wives in your reality TV neighborhood.
 Pretty much every woman on the series, in Utah and in Orange County, is an online influencer, content creator or personality. MomTok was the friend group of young female TikTokers in Utah from which the original series was largely cast.
 Many of them were internet-famous long before they appeared on TV. And most of them are apparently making a whole lot of money from their jobs, to the point that one of the most common issues in their marriages is that the wives are more successful than the husbands.
 The majority of the Orange County wives are married, and almost all of them married young, many in their teens. Now, in their late 20s and early 30s, most have at least a couple of kids, with some of the older ones – 36 is the oldest of the Orange County wives – having up to four or five kids.
 As for their Mormon bona fides, well, it’s possible that their connections to the faith might be more loosely defined than Joseph Smith or Brigham Young might have imagined. You definitely won’t find “soft swinging” – non-monogamous physical intimacy that didn’t go all the way – in the Book of Mormon.
 As for the Orange County cast, the eight wives are about equally divided between those who are practicing Mormons and those who are not.
 Now that the basics are out of the way, let’s meet the cast.
 Jen Affleck , 27, is the only cast member to cross over from the original series to the spinoff. As such, she opens the series as a kind of narrator for the new show. She and her husband Zac have been in rocky waters for some time. Her idea about moving to California was to try a reset for the family.
 Jen’s still thinking about leaving Zac, but by the end of the second episode we learn that might not be so easy.
 Aspyn Ovard , 30, is recently divorced from her high school sweetheart Parker, and already in a new relationship … with a woman … and the woman’s husband. That’s right, we’ve got Orange County reality TV wives’ first-ever throuple with Aspyn, Bri and Billy all livin’ and lovin’ together.
 This confuses some of the wives. First, they struggle just pronouncing “polyamory,” and then try to figure out how it’s similar or different to the polygamy practiced before the Church of Latter-Day Saints banned it many years ago.
 But the big reveal and the heaviest moment of the opening episodes comes when Aspyn breaks down in therapy with Parker and reveals to viewers that one of their daughters is terminally ill with cancer.
 Salomé Andrea , 34, has twin daughters with husband Aaron, to whom she’s been married 17 years. Minus the one year they were separated and headed for divorce before deciding to try once more to make it work. Within weeks of getting back together, Salomé discovered she’s pregnant, which is where her story begins on the series.
 Aaron knows most of the men Salomé dated during their break – one of them is Chase McWhorter, the estranged husband of Miranda Hope, a wife on the original series. Salomé does not know any of the women with whom Aaron dated and it’s an issue for her.
 McCall DaPron , 36, is the self-appointed leader of the wives. She’s also the most religious of the bunch. Having converted her husband and her best friend to Mormonism, she talks repeatedly about how she can convert anyone. McCall, whose younger sister Mayci Neeley is on the original show, is already getting under the skin of half the wives.
 Bobbi Althoff , 29, is a successful podcaster, co-hosting “The Really Good Show,” on which she’s interviewed celebrities including Drake, Mark Cuban, Shaquille O’Neal and other celebrities. She was born in Moreno Valley and grew up in Perris. And she’s not and has never been a Mormon. Her brother converted, and she had friends in high school, but she’s really more Mormon-adjacent.
 She’s got a dark sense of humor and a no-flips-given attitude. Before the girls’ trip to Palm Springs in episode two, she impresses Salomé and Avery when she texts Wiz Khalifa to arrange some killer weed to take the edge off McCall’s relentless Queen Bee-dom.
 Avery Woods , 31, is also not Mormon, but grew up in Mesa, Arizona, with many Mormon friends. She’s a pediatric intensive-care nurse turned podcaster and influencer and seems to have the most extensive, definitely-not-Mormon-approved vocabulary of any of the wives. She’s good friends with Bobbi and Salomé, whose sometimes fourth-wheel is Aspyn of the throuple.
 Madison Bontempo , 34, like McCall, grew up in Orange County. She’s got five children with husband Kyler, and while she follows most of the rules of the church she admits in one episode that she wouldn’t mind breaking a few of them. The idea of a marijuana edible is her example of one that intrigues.
 Ashleigh Pease , 32, and Jordan McClanahan , 36, are the other two members of McCall’s active Mormon crew. Ashleigh’s from Australia originally, while Jordan is from Orange County, where, like McCall and Madison, she attended Tesoro High School in Rancho Santa Margarita.
 Neither Ashleigh nor Jordan made a strong impression in the first two episodes, though Jordan does seem to have replaced Chandler Higginson as a regular cast member, bumping Chandler, who was announced in April as part of the show, down to Friend of the Mormon Wives status.
 Now you know a little about them; stay tuned for more high-and-low lights as seen in the trailer for the season to unfold.
